lines: N
When people work side by side, a glance or a gesture is often enough to be understood.

vis: 第三人称：用户戴上 Vision Pro 站在书架前
lines: N
Can an AI assistant that sees through our eyes collaborate the same way?

vis: 用户拿起书又放回，犹豫不决
lines: N
Imagine organizing a crowded family bookshelf, with Dad's classics, your sister's picture books, and your own textbooks, helped by an AI assistant in your glasses.
N
Today's assistants make you translate what you see and do into words. Rich, parallel physical intent gets squeezed into a single verbal channel. This is the communication gulf.
N

And even when the AI recognizes objects, it misses embodied cues, like a hesitant gaze or a pause with a book in hand, and it forgets the personal rules you just agreed on. This is the understanding gulf.
N
So we ask: how can a shared first-person perspective enable continuous cognitive alignment between humans and AI?
N
We introduce Eye2Eye, a framework that turns the first-person view from a passive input into a shared channel for collaboration. It closes a loop of three components.
We introduce Eye-to-Eye, a framework that turns the first-person view from a passive input into a shared channel for collaboration. It closes a loop of three components.
N
One: joint attention. From human to AI, Eye2Eye captures speech, gaze, and gestures such as pointing, touching, and grasping, to detect interaction events and infer intent.
One: joint attention. From human to AI, Eye-to-Eye captures speech, gaze, and gestures such as pointing, touching, and grasping, to detect interaction events and infer intent.
label: I · Joint Attention

vis: Vision Pro 第一人称录屏：AI 对目标物体的高亮框 + 文字标签
lines: N
From AI to human, it makes its own focus visible through visual highlights, voice, and text labels, so both partners converge on the same object.
label: I · AI → Human

lines: N

Two: accumulated common ground. Each interaction is stored in a dynamic object card: what the object is, what the user intended, how the AI responded, and whether it worked. Cards persist, and they are revised whenever the AI is corrected.
label: II · Common Ground

lines: N

Three: reflective situated feedback. Using that common ground, the AI picks one of four strategies: object recognition, error checking, knowledge recall, or action planning, each mixing visual and verbal cues. It then watches how the user reacts, and writes the outcome back to memory.
label: III · Situated Feedback

lines: N
Together, these components form a continuous perceive, align, and reflect loop.
N

Our prototype runs on Apple Vision Pro. YOLO tracks objects in the first-person view. When a hand overlaps an object, or gaze dwells on it for six seconds, an event fires, and GPT-4o interprets the frame together with the user's speech.
label: Joint Attention pipeline

lines: N
That state is embedded and matched against existing object cards by cosine similarity. The best match is retrieved, fused with the current state, and the card is created or updated.
label: Object-card memory (RAG)

lines: N
Finally, the model selects a feedback strategy and modality, rendered in AR and spoken with Gemini text-to-speech, in about four to five seconds end to end.
label: Feedback generation

lines: N
Beyond bookshelves, the same loop guides procedural tasks like operating a coffee machine, and inspection tasks like troubleshooting a circuit board.
label: Also: coffee machine · circuit board

lines: N
We compared Eye2Eye with a baseline using the same headset and models, in a study with sixty participants and three tasks.
We compared Eye-to-Eye with a baseline using the same headset and models, in a study with sixty participants and three tasks.
N
Eye2Eye reduced the likelihood of errors by about fifty-eight percent, cut clarification turns by half, and reduced interaction turns in the procedural task by twenty-three percent.
Eye-to-Eye reduced the likelihood of errors by about fifty-eight percent, cut clarification turns by half, and reduced interaction turns in the procedural task by twenty-three percent.
N
Errors also accumulated far more slowly over time, and participants rated the collaboration as significantly more fluent, more co-present, and more trustworthy.
